mission: Departure from the Battlefield Node — group processes what they've learned, decides next stop. Ben grapples privately with the institutional lie's growing weight.
why_now: Each Corridor stop adds to the moral burden — Ben must carry both the crisis and the cover-up
conflict: Ben drafts another partial report to Luke — more context, still not the full truth. The gap between what he knows and what he reports widens.
turning_point: Torin finds Ben composing the report and asks simply: 'What will you tell them?' Not accusatory — curious. Ben changes the subject. The question hangs.
opening_hook: Ben hunches over his datapad composing the second partial report to Luke — enough to explain the delay, not enough to reveal the scope — while the thin place's effects fade like a headache lifting
closing_hook: Next node on approach. This one's degradation is worse — the Force ahead feels intermittent rather than merely offset. And the energy signature Desh flagged? It's stronger here. Much stronger. Someone spent time.
emotional_trajectory: Reflective processing -> the weight of withholding -> renewed determination

stakes.personal: Ben's integrity eroding with each incomplete report
stakes.interpersonal: Torin's question about honesty — foreshadowing his own relationship with truth
stakes.external: The next stop shows heavier Veraine activity

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — Ben's makeshift workspace, then cockpit
sensory_details: The datapad with Luke's comm frequency; Torin's presence in the doorway — warm, heavy, his Force signature slightly wrong in a way Ben can't name; nav display showing the next node's degraded readings
action_beats: Ben drafts another partial report to Luke on his datapad, editing out the full scope before transmitting
Torin leans against the doorframe of Ben's makeshift workspace and watches him compose the message
Desh pulls up the next node's readings on the nav display — energy signature registering stronger than the last
notes: SP4 (institutional lie) advancing — Ben's withholding from Luke is a mirror of the Order's thousand-year amnesia. Torin's question is a soft hook-adjacent moment — not registered as a formal hook but adds to his long-burn characterization.
